title: Strict transform commutes with affine pushforward
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent], and let $b:S^b=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(S)\to S$ be its blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an affine morphism of $S$-schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $g_b:X\times_SS^b\to Y\times_SS^b$ for the base change [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $\mathcal F^b$ denotes the module strict transform relative to $\mathcal I$ [def-trf-module-strict-transform], then there is a canonical isomorphism $g_{b,*}\mathcal F^b\cong(g_*\mathcal F)^b$ of $\mathcal O_{Y\times_SS^b}$-modules.

proof.text: Put $X_b=X\times_SS^b$, $Y_b=Y\times_SS^b$, and let $p_X,p_Y$ be their projections. The universal property identifies $X_b=X\times_YY_b$, so affine permanence makes $g_b$ affine. Affine base change gives $g_*\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent and $\beta:H_Y=p_Y^*g_*\mathcal F\simeq g_{b,*}H_X$, where $H_X=p_X^*\mathcal F$. Tensor pullback makes both $H_X,H_Y$ quasi-coherent; no flatness is needed.

Let $q_X:X_b\to S^b$, $q_Y:Y_b\to S^b$ be the projections, let $E=b^{-1}V(\mathcal I)$ be the closed subscheme cut out by $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{S^b}$, and put $D_X=q_X^{-1}E$, $D_Y=q_Y^{-1}E$; as $q_X=q_Y\circ g_b$, $D_X=g_b^{-1}D_Y$. Principalization makes $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{S^b}$ locally principal, so $E$ is a locally principal closed subscheme. Apply the locally-principal supported-kernel lemma to $(q_X,E,H_X)$ and $(q_Y,E,H_Y)$: the open inclusions $j_X,j_Y$ of $X_b\setminus D_X$, $Y_b\setminus D_Y$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, even if an equation becomes a zero divisor. Since $j_X^{-1}W=W\setminus D_X$, both complements are retrocompact.

proof.text: The supported-sections theorem applied to $(X_b,D_X,H_X)$ gives its quasi-coherent subsheaf $K_X$ of sections zero off $D_X$, with the affine ideal-power description. The cokernel theorem gives $Q_X=H_X/K_X$ quasi-coherent. The strict-transform definition identifies $Q_X=\mathcal F^b$.

Affineness of $g_b$ implies quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Apply the supported-pushforward lemma with $(f,Z,\mathcal F)=(g_b,D_Y,H_X)$; Step 2 supplies retrocompactness. Under $\beta$ this identifies $g_{b,*}K_X$ with the subsheaf $K_Y\subseteq H_Y$ of sections zero off $D_Y$.

source.place: Tag 07ZQ, lemma-push-sections-supported-on-closed-subset, statement and hint (3904--3923); quasi-coherence via Tag 07ZP.

proof.text: Apply the affine quotient lemma to $(g_b,K_X\subseteq H_X)$, using Step 3 for quasi-coherence. It gives the canonical isomorphism $\theta:(g_{b,*}H_X)/(g_{b,*}K_X)\xrightarrow{\sim}g_{b,*}Q_X$ satisfying $\theta\pi=g_{b,*}(H_X\to Q_X)$, and makes this last map epic.

source.place: Tag 080G, lemma-strict-transform-affine, final sentence (8930--8932); general affine quotient argument, with Schemes Tags 01IB, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent, and 01IC, lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent.

proof.text: By Step 4, $\beta^{-1}$ induces $\bar\beta^{-1}:(g_{b,*}H_X)/(g_{b,*}K_X)\simeq H_Y/K_Y$, inverse to the map induced by $\beta$ (their composites are identity before quotienting). Compose $\theta^{-1}$ with it. The quotient definitions identify the result with $g_{b,*}\mathcal F^b\simeq(g_*\mathcal F)^b$. It commutes with the original quotient maps; the epimorphism of Step 5 makes this compatibility determine it uniquely, proving canonicity.
